description: Generalized past-time detection (audit commit ad3641395). The hasPastTimeMarker helper drives rule en-yesterday-irregular-beginner-past, which rewrites a beginner present-tense irregular verb (buy/do/eat/go/have) to its past form ONLY when a recognized past-time marker is present AND a (subject pronoun + target verb) adjacency exists. The audit's negation lookahead (?!\s+not\b) keeps it from mangling negated past. Expectations encode the VERIFIED behaviour of correctWithTutorRules() on current main.
fp_risk_note: Past-time detection has the broadest false-positive surface in the audit set, and Lane A has since broadened the marker regex (now recognizing 'on <weekday>', 'in <year>', '<n> hour(s) ago', 'last summer' in addition to the original yesterday/last-<unit>/<n>-<unit>-ago set). That widening raises the FP risk, so the negative cases stress: (1) future markers that look temporal — 'tomorrow', 'next week', future modal 'will go'; (2) already-correct past where a marker is present but no (pronoun + target-verb) adjacency exists — e.g. conditional 'would have gone yesterday'; (3) idioms not recognized as markers — 'back in the day'; (4) nested / possessive time references — "Yesterday's homework is due tomorrow"; (5) the negation guard, where 'do not' must NOT be rewritten and the engine escalates to needs_ai. The former coverage-gap markers (on <weekday>/in <year>/an hour ago/last summer) are now covered and live in positive[]; a regression that re-widens the regex without re-checking the negatives will turn future/idiom/possessive sentences into wrong rewrites.

positive.notes: Standard past-tense verb correction after 'yesterday' (go -> went).

negative.notes: FP-stress (negation guard): (?!\s+not\b) blocks the 'do -> did' rewrite, so the rule produces no change and the engine escalates to needs_ai rather than emitting a wrong fix.
